items.title: Girl's suspected abductor had been out of jail for just six days, police say
items.description: Northern Territory Police believe five-year-old Sharon Granites was abducted from a home in an Alice Springs town camp as the search continues into its third day.

items.title: Global defence spending hits record high. This is how countries rank
items.description: The world is spending more money on weapons than ever before, reaching nearly $4 trillion in 2025.

items.title: Donald Trump names new ambassador to Australia
items.description: The Trump administration has nominated former congressman David Brat as ambassador to Australia.

items.title: 'Almost bullying': Private hospitals blame closures on 'cowboy' insurers
items.description: A former Bupa executive accuses health insurers of using "almost bullying" tactics in their negotiations with private hospitals, while the Australian Private Hospitals Association says insurers have become "cowboys" in need of regulation.

items.title: 'You're lying': Rebel Wilson denies evidence is a 'grotesque pretence'
items.description: The Hollywood star is being sued for defamation in the Federal Court by Charlotte MacInnes, who plays the lead actor in Ms Wilson's debut directorial film The Deb.

items.title: Coalition points to stealth bombers as potential AUKUS stop-gap
items.description: The Coalition says Australia should consider buying next-generation stealth bombers to help bridge the gap until the AUKUS submarines arrive.

items.title: Jimmy Kimmel says joke misconstrued as Trumps call to fire late-night host
items.description: Donald Trump says Jimmy Kimmel should be fired for a monologue he delivered days before the third alleged attempt to assassinate the US president.

items.title: Affidavit reveals more details as man charged with attempted Trump assassination
items.description: The man accused of opening fire at a Washington dinner attended by Donald Trump has been charged with attempting to assassinate the US president and could face life in prison if convicted.

items.title: A simple message of love: Memorial held at Port Arthur 30 years on from the massacre
items.description: Thirty years on from the Port Arthur tragedy, survivor Jane Scholefield had a simple message for those still bearing the scars of that day — keep love at the centre of mourning.

items.title: Man who randomly killed British tourist not criminally responsible
items.description: A man who killed a British tourist in a random stabbing at an Albury motel in 2024 has been found not criminally responsible for the attack.

items.title: Police to investigate groups 'pulling the strings' in Melbourne firebombings
items.description: Police are investigating whether recent arson attacks across 15 Melbourne hospitality venues are linked to an organised crime syndicate.

items.title: No inspections allowed, bids to start at $1 for seven-storey 'eyesore'
items.description: Rockhampton's Plaza Hotel is set to go under the hammer after closing down more than a decade ago.

items.title: Electric ferry needs a lift as transport ship stuck in Strait of Hormuz
items.description: The world's largest electric ferry is sitting idle in Tasmania after construction was completed because the heavy-lift ship that was booked to take it to South America is stuck in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: NRL's greatest ever try-scorer hints at imminent PNG switch
items.description: Record-setting South Sydney try-scoring winger Alex Johnston looks set to become the first player to sign for the PNG Chiefs ahead of their 2028 NRL entry.

items.title: The soy sauce fish is a perfect design — except on one important point
items.description: Shoyu-tai, the single-use plastic soy sauce fish that accompany takeaway sushi, are an eco-nightmare — but a local designer has a solution.

items.title: How to live on other mobs' Country, respectfully
items.description: To better understand what respect looks like in practice, I spoke with other First Nations people about how they approach working and living on other mobs' Countries.

items.title: The moment Andy Lee feared exploits with Hamish Blake had gone too far
items.description: Andy Lee opens up on his 23-year working relationship with his "fast and loose" comedy partner Hamish Blake, and the stunt that left him fearing for his mate's life.

items.title: Police honour Kalgoorlie detectives brutally killed 100 years ago
items.description: On this day in 1926, Detective Inspector John Walsh and Detective Sergeant Alexander Pitman were shot while trying to apprehend gold thieves near Kalgoorlie. Their charred and dismembered bodies were later found at the bottom of a mine shaft.

items.title: Bus driver had 'microsleep' before fatal crash, jury hears
items.description: The first police officers to arrive on the scene of a fatal bus crash in north Queensland have told the court of their conversations with the driver in the immediate aftermath of the incident.

items.title: NSW public transport Opal network is set to change. Here's what we know
items.description: Digital cards, fresh Opal readers, real-time information and the end of "phantom buses" are being flagged as part of a planned $820 million upgrade to the New South Wales public transport network.

items.title: Protester who dumped shark heads at minister's office willing to go to jail
items.description: Bunbury fisherman Mason Jones, who led a protest against the WA government's demersal fishing ban, says he has no intention of stopping the campaign.

items.title: Commuters warned rail disruptions could worsen ahead of Magic Round
items.description: Queensland Rail says it put a "new and improved" offer to the Fair Work Commission on Monday night, which the Rail, Tram and Bus Union (RTBU) has labelled "pitiful".

items.title: 'How the hell?' Millie Elliott bounced straight back into Origin post-baby
items.description: Millie Elliott could have taken an easy route back into competitive action after having a baby. Instead, she is throwing herself straight back into the State of Origin cauldron on Thursday night.

items.title: Rock climber dies after fall at Organ Pipes near Mount Arapiles
items.description: The woman was climbing with a group of other climbers at Organ Pipes near Mount Arapiles yesterday.

items.title: Tourist drowns at popular West Australian beach
items.description: Police say the man, a tourist visiting from South-East Asia with his family, was swept from the rocks at Indijup Natural Spa near Yallingup on Monday.
